# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

items.t: Fill in your name exactly as on Aadhaar and EPIC, the address, district, block and phone number.
Upload both sides of your voter ID, and Aadhaar if you have it, then submit. The request goes to the SHA office for approval.
Once it is approved (check on the toll-free number or at the kiosk), visit the District Kiosk with the original EPIC, Aadhaar and relation proofs. Each member gets an individual MHIS/PMJAY card.
At the hospital, hand the card and any government photo ID to the Arogya Mitra at the MHIS counter. Treatment is cashless. If you lose the card, a new one is printed at any District Kiosk.
1800 102 4762 — MHIS toll-free / 0364-250 7477 — MHIS helpdesk / 14555 — Ayushman Bharat national helpline
Mizoram Universal Health Care Scheme (MUHCS Card)
Mizoram State Health Care Society, Department of Health & Family Welfare, Government of Mizoram

From 1 April 2025 MUHCS replaced the old Mizoram State Health Care Scheme (MSHCS), and it covers every bona fide resident of Mizoram. Families outside government service pay a yearly fee of Rs.2,500, Rs.5,000 or Rs.10,000 for Rs.5 lakh of cashless hospital cover; the higher fee buys a better ward, while AB PM-JAY (Golden Card) families pay nothing and government employees pay monthly from their salary. The paid enrolment opens once a year (for 2026-27 it ran from 16 February to 15 May 2026), mostly online, with offline forms at sub-centres where there is no internet. After that you apply for the MUHCS card online and download it once approved.
Rs.5 lakh a year per family, cashless, for a yearly family fee of Rs.2,500, Rs.5,000 or Rs.10,000
Every bona fide resident of Mizoram listed in the state ration card (PDS) database
General families pay a yearly fee: Rs.2,500 (general ward), Rs.5,000 (semi-private shared ward) or Rs.10,000 (private ward). The cover is Rs.5 lakh in each plan
AB PM-JAY (Golden Card) families pay nothing and use their Golden Card. They do not need a MUHCS card
State government employees and provisional or muster roll staff pay Rs.200 to Rs.1,500 a month from their salary, by pay level. They do not enrol, they only make the card
Civil pensioners and GIA employees are covered through their subscription form, but the MUHCS card is not yet issued to them (circular of 13 May 2026)
Children under 5 use a parent's card. The fee is paid only in the yearly enrolment window and is not refunded except as notified
Ration card. Without one, a Village Council or Local Council letter listing the family members
A clear chest-up photo of each member, to upload for the card
UPI, debit or credit card, or net banking, to pay the yearly fee (general families)
Your own working number. The OTP comes here every time you log in.
Type the letters shown in the picture, then the OTP sent to your phone.
The family is taken from the ration card. Without one, upload the Village or Local Council letter.
Standard Rs.5,000 gives a shared semi-private ward, Private Rs.10,000 a private ward. The cover is Rs.5 lakh in all three.
Every member aged 5 or above needs their own Aadhaar for the card.
Clear, face straight, from the chest up. A blurred photo gets the card rejected.
Pay online and keep the receipt. You need it for any later query or refund request.
During the yearly enrolment window (for 2026-27 it was 16 February to 15 May 2026), open the MUHCS portal, choose Beneficiary and log in with your mobile number, the captcha and the OTP.
Enter your ration card details, add all family members and choose a plan: General Rs.2,500, Standard Rs.5,000 or Private Rs.10,000.
Pay the fee online by UPI, card or net banking and save the receipt. In villages without internet, fill in the offline form at the health sub-centre instead.
Apply for the MUHCS card from the same login. Upload each member's Aadhaar and a clear chest-up photo. Children under 5 do not need a card.
The Mizoram State Health Care Society checks and approves the request. Then log in again and download the card.
At an empanelled government or private hospital, show the MUHCS card (or your Golden Card) and get cashless treatment up to Rs.5 lakh. Re-enrol every year in the window.
08065293906 — MUHCS Chhawntu call centre / 0389-2328223 — Mizoram State Health Care Society office / 7628839899 — MUHCS grievance / 14555 — Ayushman Bharat toll-free
Chief Minister Health Insurance Scheme (CMHIS Card)
Nagaland Health Protection Society, Department of Health & Family Welfare, Government of Nagaland

Nagaland's own health insurance, run together with PM-JAY as AB PM-JAY CMHIS: the General Category gives Rs.5 lakh a year per family of cashless hospital treatment to indigenous inhabitants and permanent residents who are not covered by PM-JAY. Government employees and pensioners get Rs.20 lakh. A family registers online on the CMHIS portal or at a registration centre, the district administration approves it, and the Ayushman CMHIS card is then made after Aadhaar e-KYC at a centre. Registration is free.
Rs.5 lakh a year per family (General Category); Rs.20 lakh for government employees and pensioners
Indigenous inhabitants or permanent residents of Nagaland not covered by AB PM-JAY or any other public health insurance (General Category)
Contractual, ad-hoc and fixed-pay state employees with a valid PIMS code, and accredited journalists, also come under the General Category
Regular state government employees, legislators, PSU employees and pensioners, with their dependants, come under CMHIS (EP) with Rs.20 lakh cover
Ration card holders need not register as a new household. Their card is made against the existing ration card
A household means people who live together and share one kitchen. There is no income limit
Indigenous Inhabitant Certificate (IIC) or Permanent Resident Certificate (PRC) issued after 2016, for the head of the household
System-generated self-declaration form, signed by the applicant and the Village, Ward or Colony Chairman
Aadhaar card of every member, for e-KYC
A mobile number and an email ID (both verified by OTP)
Proof of relationship for every dependant except the spouse
Employees: PIMS code. Pensioners: PPO number and the first 3 pages of the PPO book as a PDF

Verified by OTP. You will log in with it later.

Everyone who lives with you and shares one kitchen.
Needed for every dependant except the spouse.

Open the CMHIS registration page and choose General Category. Employees use their PIMS code, pensioners their PPO number.
Enter your full name as on Aadhaar, and verify your mobile number and email with the OTPs.
Add your household members and upload the IIC or PRC and the relationship proofs. Download the self-declaration form, get it signed by the Village, Ward or Colony Chairman, and upload it.
Submit. The district administration that issued your IIC or PRC checks it. On approval you get an SMS and email with your Household ID.

Take the Household ID and every member's Aadhaar to a registration centre (district hospital, CHC, PHC, DC office or CSC) for Aadhaar e-KYC, and collect the Ayushman CMHIS card. Ration card holders can go straight to this step.
At an empanelled hospital, show the card. Treatment is cashless up to Rs.5 lakh a year for the family.
1800 202 3380 — CMHIS helpdesk, Nagaland Health Protection Society / 14555 — Ayushman Bharat national helpline
Women & Child Development Department, Government of Odisha (with the Union Ministry of Women & Child Development for PMMVY)

Cash help for a pregnant woman so she can eat well and rest before and after the birth. Since 1 April 2025 Odisha's old Mamata scheme and the central PMMVY run together as MAMATA-PMMVY, and the amount has gone up to Rs 10,000 for a boy and Rs 12,000 for a girl. It is paid in two instalments, for the first two live births (all births for PVTG families), straight into the mother's Aadhaar-linked account. You register at your Anganwadi Centre; the Anganwadi worker fills the form on the scheme's app, or you can self-register on the app.
Rs 10,000 for a boy, Rs 12,000 for a girl, in two instalments (first two live births)
Pregnant women and new mothers living in Odisha, aged 18 years 7 months to 55 years on the date of the last period (LMP)

Must fit any one: SC or ST; 40% or more disability; ration card; Ayushman (PMJAY) card; e-Shram card; woman farmer getting PM-KISAN; MGNREGA job card; family income below Rs 8 lakh; or Anganwadi worker, helper or ASHA
Paid for the first two live births. Women of the 13 PVTG communities (Bonda, Juang, Dongria Kondh, Lanjia Saora and others) get it for every birth, until March 2029
Not for women whose own or husband's job is a regular Central or State government or PSU post, or whose family income is above Rs 8 lakh
First instalment: pregnancy registered at the Anganwadi and at least one check-up (ANC) within six months of the last period. Second: birth registered and all the baby's vaccines up to 14 weeks done
Bank or post office account in her name only, linked to Aadhaar and DBT-enabled, with a photocopy of the passbook's first page
Mobile number linked to Aadhaar and the bank account
Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card, given free by the ANM when the pregnancy is registered
One proof of eligibility: caste certificate, disability certificate, Ayushman card, PM-KISAN, income certificate, ration card, e-Shram card, MGNREGA job card, or Anganwadi/ASHA identity card
For the second instalment: the baby's birth registration and vaccinations entered in the MCP card

Your village or ward Anganwadi Centre. Go as soon as you know you are pregnant, within six months of your last period, and take your Aadhaar card, bank or post office passbook, mobile phone, MCP card, ABHA number and one eligibility proof (such as the ration card). The Anganwadi worker fills the form on the MAMATA-PMMVY app for you, free; you get an SMS on your phone as acknowledgement. For the second instalment, go back to the same Anganwadi Centre after the baby's 14-week vaccines.
Name of beneficiary (as on Aadhaar)
The pregnant woman's own name, spelt exactly as on her Aadhaar card.
The woman's own Aadhaar. Without it the form cannot be registered.
She must be between 18 years 7 months and 55 years on the date of the last period.
As written on the ration card or MCP card.
A number linked to her Aadhaar and bank account. The acknowledgement and payment messages come here.
The first day of the last period, as written in the MCP card. The first check-up must be within six months of this date.
Count only children born alive and living. The scheme pays for the first two births (all births for PVTG families).
MCP card number and ANC check-up date
From the MCP card the ANM gave you. If the check-up was done elsewhere, show the doctor's slip with the date.
Any one of the listed proofs is enough, for example the ration card, Ayushman card or job card.
A single-holder account in her own name, linked to Aadhaar. Money goes to the account linked last to her Aadhaar.
As soon as you know you are pregnant, register at the Anganwadi Centre, get the MCP card from the ANM, and have at least one check-up within six months of the last period.
Give the Anganwadi worker your Aadhaar, passbook, mobile number, MCP card, ABHA number and one eligibility proof. She registers you on the MAMATA-PMMVY app, and an SMS confirms the application.
After verification by the ICDS project office, the first instalment of Rs 6,000 comes by DBT into your Aadhaar-linked account.
Have the baby, get the birth registered at the health centre or Anganwadi, and complete all vaccines up to 14 weeks (at birth, 6, 10 and 14 weeks), all entered in the MCP card.
The Anganwadi worker sends the claim for the second instalment: Rs 4,000 more for a boy or Rs 6,000 more for a girl, again straight to your account.
Ask the Anganwadi worker for the status, or check it on the app. If money is late, tell the Anganwadi worker or the CDPO, or call 181.
181 (Mamata and women's helpline, toll-free) / 1515 (PMMVY toll-free helpline)
Department of Agriculture & Farmers' Empowerment, Government of Odisha (Directorate of Agriculture & Food Production)

Odisha's own cash help for farmers, which replaced the KALIA scheme in September 2024. Small and marginal farmers get Rs 4,000 a year, Rs 2,000 before each crop season, on top of PM-KISAN's Rs 6,000, so most get Rs 10,000 a year in all. Landless farm-labour households in villages get Rs 12,500 in three instalments to start goat, poultry, duck, fishery, mushroom, bee or dairy work. One online registration on the CM KISAN portal covers both CM-KISAN and PM-KISAN, and from July 2026 an AgriStack Farmer ID is required.
Rs 4,000 a year (Rs 2,000 per crop season) for small and marginal farmers; Rs 12,500 in three instalments for landless households
Small and marginal farmers, including sharecroppers who actually till the land, who are permanent residents of Odisha
Landless agricultural households in villages who live mainly on farm work, with an MGNREGA job card
Applicant must be 18 or older, and the family must hold a valid ration card. Only one member per family is paid; the family is worked out from the ration card
Land must be registered on Krushak Odisha, and an AgriStack Farmer ID is needed to register
Medium and large farmers get only PM-KISAN through the same portal, not CM-KISAN
Not for families with an income-tax payer, a government or PSU employee or pensioner, a present or former MP, MLA or minister, or a registered doctor, engineer, lawyer, CA or architect
Bank passbook first page; the savings account must be linked to Aadhaar
Land record (RoR) registered on Krushak Odisha, for small and marginal farmers
MGNREGA job card, for landless agricultural households
A mobile number of your own that no other applicant has used
Your own Aadhaar. A wrong or someone else's Aadhaar gets the application rejected. e-KYC is by OTP, or by fingerprint at a CSC or post office.
A number in your own use that no other farmer has registered with. The OTP and payment messages come here.
The farmer ID you got when your land was added to the Farmer Registry. Ask the Village Agriculture Worker if you do not have one.
Choose Landless Agricultural Household (LAH) if you own no farm land but work on farms.
Your family's ration card number. Only one person from a ration card can get CM-KISAN.
These come up from your Krushak Odisha record. Check that the khata and plot are really yours before going on.
The money goes only to the account linked to your Aadhaar. Get it linked at your branch first.
Clear photos or scans. Landless households upload the MGNREGA job card instead of the RoR.
Before applying, register your land on Krushak Odisha and get your AgriStack Farmer ID (the Village Agriculture Worker or a CSC helps), and link Aadhaar to your bank account at the branch.
Open cmkisan.odisha.gov.in and click Farmer Registration. Read the instructions, tick the declaration, then verify your Aadhaar and mobile number with OTP.
Choose your category, fill in the ration card, address, land and bank details, upload the documents and submit. Note the token number shown.

The application is checked by the Village Agriculture Worker, the Block Agriculture Officer and the Chief District Agriculture Officer, and the Collector gives final approval. If a paper is wrong, the VAW sends it back for you to correct.
Track it under Check Status and e-KYC Status on the same portal, using the token number or Aadhaar.

Once approved, Rs 2,000 comes by DBT before the Kharif season (around Akshaya Tritiya) and Rs 2,000 before the Rabi season (around Nuakhai). PM-KISAN money comes separately from the same registration.
155333 (Krushi Samrudhi Helpline, Agriculture Department) / 155261 or 1800-115-526 (PM-KISAN helpline)
Nirman Shramik Registration — OB&OCWW Board (Construction Worker Card)
Odisha Building & Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board, Labour & ESI Department, Government of Odisha

Registers a construction worker with the Odisha welfare board and gives an identity card with a registration number. After one year on the register, the worker and family can claim the board's help: Rs 10,000 for each of two deliveries for women workers, Rs 50,000 for a daughter's or her own marriage, Rs 2,000 to Rs 40,000 a year for two children's studies, up to Rs 3 lakh for major illness, tools and bicycle money, and Rs 2 lakh (Rs 4 lakh if killed at work) to the family on death. Registration costs Rs 20 plus Rs 50 a year, and is done online on the NirmanShramik portal.
Worker card for board help — Rs 10,000 maternity, Rs 50,000 marriage, Rs 2,000–40,000 a year education, Rs 2–4 lakh death benefit
Building or construction worker who has completed 18 years and not yet 60
At least 90 days of building or other construction work in the last 12 months
Not working in a factory or mine covered by the Factories Act or the Mines Act
Not a member of any other welfare fund, and not registered with another district or state's construction board
Workers from Odisha working in other states can also register
Pay Rs 50 every year to stay a member; missing three years in a row ends membership. Most benefits start after one year of registration
